subject: Citrine Financial — urgent: SLO drift and output quality after v5/quant deploy
messages:
From: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@citrine-fin.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@citrine-fin.com
Date: 2027-01-10T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: production model upgrade (v5 + q2) — severe latency & bad outputs

Vanessa — we pushed your v5 + quant profile q2 last night (per schedule) and since 02:00 UTC we're seeing p95/p99 jump ~2.5x and error rate up 7x. Downstream sampling shows hallucinations on payment descriptions (two merchant names attributed to single transaction). This is breaking reconciliation jobs and triggering fraud rules.

Attached: p99_trace_20270110.log and a small sample_responses_20270110.jsonl with examples. Can you confirm a rollback or immediate mitigation? We need TTL restoration within 6 hours or we'll have to throttle traffic.

—Alex
Head of Platform, Citrine Financial

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@citrine-fin.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T08:33:00Z
Subject: Re: production model upgrade (v5 + q2) — severe latency & bad outputs

Alex — thank you for the fast heads up and the traces. I'm escalating to runtime and inference ops now (cc'ed). Initial read: p99 and errors line up with the new quant profile for v5 (q2). We can enact an immediate fallback to the v4.q1 variant for traffic routing — that will restore latency and reduce divergence while we investigate.

Immediate plan: 1) IOPs will flip routing to v4.q1 within the hour (target 60m). 2) We'll capture a 1h post-fallback sample and compare quality. 3) I'll loop in Marcus for exec visibility & credit discussion.

Will confirm when rollback is live.

—Vanessa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T08:55:00Z
Subject: Re: production model upgrade (v5 + q2) — severe latency & bad outputs

Marked priority P0. I'm taking runtime lead. Notes from quick triage: q2 reduces compute precision on final decode kernel which increases per-token compute variability on long request paths (payments text tends to be 180-300 tokens). We also see a KV cache eviction pattern for the hot client prefixes which worsens latency spikes. Initiating traffic split: 0% to v5.q2 -> 100% v4.q1. Will post ops timeline.

Attachments referenced in loop: p99_trace_20270110.log (parsing now).

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@citrine-fin.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: production model upgrade (v5 + q2) — severe latency & bad outputs

Alex — routing rollback to v4.q1 completed at 2027-01-10T09:37Z. Live metrics show p95 back within 10% of baseline and p99 trending down. We're collecting quality samples now. Can you confirm whether you want a controlled canary (10% for 2h) while we instrument additional logging, or keep v4.q1 until we finish a deeper QA pass?

Also, we opened JIRA-RW-4921 to track root cause and next steps. Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Citrine-Incident-20270110

From: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@citrine-fin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: production model upgrade (v5 + q2) — severe latency & bad outputs

Thanks — confirmed rollback. For now keep v4.q1. We absolutely need: 1) a short RCA with the memory/kv eviction hypothesis, 2) the collection of the malformed outputs and confidence scores, and 3) an ETA for a safe re-introduction plan. We're briefing our CTO in 2 hours. Appreciate quick updates.

—Alex

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@citrine-fin.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-13T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Citrine — executive summary & remediation charter

Alex / team — Marcus from Product Ops. I saw the timeline and appreciate the quick rollback. We're committing to a formal remediation charter: 1) Immediate (24h): rollback confirmed, customer-facing incident note, 1h post-rollback quality dump (we'll share). 2) Short (72h): deeper triage (kernel + quant calibration + KV eviction reproduction) and mitigation (tuning q2 or an alternate quant path q2a). 3) Medium (2 weeks): validated canary plan and automated safety gates for quant-profile deployments for long-sequence workloads.

We will offer Citrine Financial a one-month credit for incidents causing SLO violation and a technical liaison through completion. Expect the 24h incident note and a draft RCA attached to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow.

I'll keep this thread active; tagging Evelyn to coordinate the credit & commercial note.

—Marcus
VP Product Operations, Redwood Inference
